correctness.rationale: A finite-rank KKT argument realizes each second-difference active-set orthogonal projector on an open input cell; polyhedral piecewise linearity reduces the global two-input Gini modulus to these local seminorms. Every input modulo constants decomposes into level-set indicator cuts with exactly additive input Gini variation, giving the precise finite formula. An included exact Fraction checker exhausts every face and complementary cut at n=2,...,8, reproduces the seven fractions and a finite KKT witness at n=4. The all-n strict lower bound follows analytically from a single curvature-active face, not from a finite experiment. Boundaries n=2,3 are included; no unproved closed expression for n>8 is asserted.

originality.rationale: Targeted comparisons with archived convex-regression source texts and two published exact results for the same Euclidean convex-cone projector found no sharp Gini modulus, four-site threshold, or the exact two-through-eight Gini sequence. The closest result is in the coordinate maximum norm, which has a different unit-ball extremal structure and first-expansive dimension. An unindexed priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed exact Gini-seminorm perturbation table for convex regression might exist under an alternative title or in a shape-restricted estimation appendix.

Earlier exact active-face algebra is directly reusable, so the novelty resides in the genuinely different all-pair norm, its sharp tabulation and first-instability boundary, not in inventing facewise projection methods.
The published full RESULT files were inspected, but exhaustive historical priority across all mathematical literature is not independently established.

value.rationale: Sharp pairwise-dispersion sensitivity of shape-constrained least squares is a natural stability invariant distinct from coordinate maximum sensitivity and stochastic squared risk. A four-site first failure, exact small-sample sequence through eight, and strict all-size amplification witness quantify a previously uncharacterized boundary. The finite-dimensional classification is motivated by the entire natural convex-sequence projector, not an arbitrary numerical slice, and the cut formula enables systematic further analysis.
